literal: His father Shao — both had great fame in the Wei age.
idiomatic: His father Shao; both father and son won great renown in Wei.

literal: Yu was mild and refined, with discernment and capacity.
idiomatic: Yu was mild and refined, with judgment and breadth of mind.

literal: Upon removing mourning he became a staff officer in the Grand Commandant's office and rose in succession to right chief clerk of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Upon removing mourning he entered service as staff officer to the grand commandant and rose in turn to right chief clerk of the secretariat.

literal: When the capital was moved to Ye, he remained behind to oversee the treasury and to transport timber from palace and temple; he was known for clarity and competence.
idiomatic: When the capital moved to Ye he stayed behind to oversee the treasury and haul palace and temple timber — and was praised for sharp, capable work.

literal: He rose in succession to Rapid Cavalry Grand General and inspector of Eastern Xu Province.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to rapid cavalry grand general and inspector of eastern Xu province.

literal: When he left his post and returned, he claimed old age and illness and sought no further office.
idiomatic: On leaving his post he went home, pleaded old age and illness, and sought no further office.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, Yu was advanced to former general concurrently and guided the rites at the Round Mound.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, Yu was promoted to former general concurrently and led the rites at the Round Mound.

literal: Yu did not wish to register his name in two dynasties; though summoned as an old acquaintance, once the affair was over he ceased court attendance.
idiomatic: Yu would not have his name entered in two dynasties; though summoned as an old friend, once the rite was done he ceased all court attendance.

literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianbao.

literal: His sons were Quan, Yun, and Song.
idiomatic: His sons were Quan, Yun, and Song.

literal: Yun was without conduct.
idiomatic: Yun was without conduct.

literal: Song gave his daughter in marriage to Huai'ao, son of Mu Tipo, and was promoted beyond measure to magistrate of Linzhang and equal in three departments.
idiomatic: Song gave his daughter to Huai'ao, son of Mu Tipo, and was promoted beyond measure to magistrate of Linzhang and equal in three departments.

literal: Yun had illicit relations with the younger sister of Lu Lingxuan; Lingxuan memorialized to appoint him crown prince attendant.
idiomatic: Yun carried on with Lu Lingxuan's younger sister; Lingxuan memorialized and had him made crown prince attendant.

literal: His younger brother Jin, styled Daoyu, whose fame is recorded in the Book of Wei.
idiomatic: His younger brother Jin, styled Daoyu, is famed in the Book of Wei.

literal: His talent and learning were praised in his age.
idiomatic: His talent and learning won praise in his age.

literal: Jin had six sons — Yanzhi, Qianzhi, Shouzhi, Lizhi, Xingzhi, and Ningzhi — all with talent and repute.
idiomatic: Jin had six sons — Yanzhi, Qianzhi, Shouzhi, Lizhi, Xingzhi, and Ningzhi — all men of talent and standing.

literal: Xingzhi was deeply affectionate with his brothers; moreover he was plain and simple in manner, and scholar-friends praised him.
idiomatic: Xingzhi loved his brothers deeply; plain and unassuming in manner, he was praised by men of letters.

literal: Fan Yang's Lu Sidao was his nephew by marriage; once he presented a poem saying: "The Director of Water Balances calls him a recluse; Pan and Yang have a marriage tie of generations; his body already shares caps and coaches, yet his mind ranges beyond the dust of the world."
idiomatic: Lu Sidao of Fan Yang was his nephew by marriage; once he sent a poem: "The Director of Water Balances calls him a recluse; Pan and Yang are kin by marriage through the generations; his body already rides with caps and coaches, yet his mind ranges beyond the dust of the world."

literal: Men of the time took this as an accurate record.
idiomatic: Men of the time took this for truth.

literal: Yu's cousin Xiao, styled Renlue.
idiomatic: Yu's cousin Xiao, styled Renlue.

literal: He was a son of Wei Grand Commandant Qian.
idiomatic: He was a son of Wei grand commandant Qian.

literal: Broad in learning, with power of thought.
idiomatic: Broad in learning, with a keen mind.

literal: Upon removing mourning he became an outer secretariat attendant.
idiomatic: Upon removing mourning he became an outer secretariat attendant.

literal: When Erzhu Rong was about to harm the court gentlemen and Xiao was to go, rats gnawed his robe and cap; he could not go and so escaped the disaster at Heyin.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was about to slaughter the court gentlemen and Xiao was to go, rats gnawed his robe and cap; he could not set out and so escaped the disaster at Heyin.

literal: When the capital moved to Ye, Xiao lodged in Qinghe and entrusted himself to his mother's sister's son Cui Juan's house.
idiomatic: When the capital moved to Ye, Xiao lodged in Qinghe at the home of his mother's sister's son, Cui Juan.

literal: He was granted thirty qing of fertile fields; Xiao then built a house and dwelt at ease, instructing and urging his nephews, with no further desire for office.
idiomatic: He was granted thirty qing of fertile land; Xiao built a house, settled in peace, and schooled his nephews — with no further wish for office.

literal: At the end of Wuding, seeing the age was at peace, he entered the capital to take office.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding, seeing the age at peace, he entered the capital to serve.

literal: He was made magistrate of Dunqiu and died in office.
idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Dunqiu and died in office.

literal: Zheng Shuzu, styled Gongwen, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
idiomatic: Zheng Shuzu, styled Gongwen, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang.

literal: His grandfather Xi was Wei director of the secretariat.
idiomatic: His grandfather Xi was Wei director of the secretariat.

literal: His father Daozhao was Wei secretariat supervisor.
idiomatic: His father Daozhao was Wei secretariat supervisor.

literal: Shuzu in youth was clever and keen, loved literary composition, had moral bearing, and was praised by elders of the age.
idiomatic: Shuzu in youth was clever and quick, loved to write, bore himself with restraint, and won praise from elders.

literal: Upon removing mourning he became a staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: Upon removing mourning he entered service as staff officer in the ministry of works.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he rose in succession to junior tutor of the crown prince, equal in three departments, and inspector of Yan Province.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he rose in turn to junior tutor of the crown prince, equal in three departments, and inspector of Yan province.

literal: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector; he sighed and said: "The ancients had a saying: 'When one hears the wind of Bo Yi, the greedy grow honest and the timid stand firm.'
idiomatic: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector; he sighed and said, "The ancients said: 'Hear the wind of Bo Yi, and the greedy grow honest; the timid stand firm.'

literal: Today I have seen it in Inspector Zheng of Yan Province."
idiomatic: Today I have seen it in Inspector Zheng of Yan province."

literal: Earlier, when Shuzu's father was at Guang Province, he built a chapel pavilion on a small hill south of the city and carved a stone inscription.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Shuzu's father held Guang province, he built a chapel on a hill south of the city and carved a stone inscription.

literal: Shuzu was then nine years old.
idiomatic: Shuzu was then nine years old.

literal: When he became inspector he went to seek the old site and found a broken stone with an inscription reading: "The White Cloud Hall of Zheng Daozhao, Mr. Zhongyue."
idiomatic: When he became inspector he went to seek the old site and found a broken stone inscribed: "The White Cloud Hall of Zheng Daozhao, Mr. Zhongyue."

literal: Shuzu faced it and sobbed; his grief moved the whole staff.
idiomatic: Shuzu faced it and sobbed aloud; his grief moved the whole staff.

literal: Someone in the market stole cloth; his father said in anger: "How can you bear to cheat the ruler!"
idiomatic: Someone in the market stole cloth; his father said in anger, "How can you bear to cheat the ruler!"

literal: He seized the man and handed him over; Shuzu especially pardoned him.
idiomatic: He seized the man and handed him over; Shuzu especially pardoned him.

literal: From then on there were no thieves within the borders.
idiomatic: From then on there were no thieves within the borders.

literal: The people sang of them: "Great Duke Zheng, little Duke Zheng — fifty years apart, yet their teaching and customs are still the same."
idiomatic: The people sang: "Great Duke Zheng, little Duke Zheng — fifty years apart, yet their teaching and customs are still one."

literal: Shuzu could play the zither and himself composed the "Dragon Chant, Ten Pieces," saying that once he dreamed a man played the zither and on waking wrote it down.
idiomatic: Shuzu could play the zither and himself composed the "Dragon Chant, Ten Pieces," saying he once dreamed a man playing the zither and on waking wrote it down.

literal: Men of the time held it matchless.
idiomatic: Men of the time held it matchless.

literal: Wherever he was posted he loved to make hills and pools, with pine and bamboo planted together.
idiomatic: Wherever he served he loved to lay out hills and pools, planting pine and bamboo together.

literal: He set out rich fare for guests and never tired of receiving them.
idiomatic: He set out rich fare for guests and never tired of welcoming them.

literal: Before he rose to honor, riding alone in the countryside, suddenly several hundred horsemen appeared; seeing Shuzu they all dismounted and said, "The lord is here," then lined up and bowed.
idiomatic: Before he rose to honor, riding alone in the countryside, suddenly several hundred horsemen appeared; seeing Shuzu they all dismounted and said, "The lord is here," then lined up and bowed.

literal: Shuzu turned to ask his attendants; none had seen them. His heart was deeply struck.
idiomatic: Shuzu turned to ask his attendants; none had seen them. His heart was deeply struck.

literal: Before long he was summoned to court and in the end held eminent rank.
idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to court and in the end held eminent rank.

literal: When gravely ill he spoke of this himself.
idiomatic: When gravely ill he spoke of this himself.

literal: He also said: "I am old now; a lifetime of wealth and honor is enough. To leave a name of integrity to my descendants — in death I have no regret."
idiomatic: He also said, "I am old now; a lifetime of wealth and honor is enough. To leave my descendants a name for integrity — in death I have no regret."

literal: He then died in the province.
idiomatic: He then died in the province.

literal: Shuzu's daughter was consort to Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui.
idiomatic: Shuzu's daughter was consort to Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui.

literal: Shuzu would sit and receive the prince's bow; only when he ordered him to sit would the prince sit.
idiomatic: Shuzu would sit and receive the prince's bow; only when Shuzu bade him sit would the prince sit.

literal: After the consort died, the prince took Zheng Daoyin's daughter in marriage.
idiomatic: After the consort died, the prince took Zheng Daoyin's daughter in marriage.

literal: The prince would sit and receive Daoyin's bow; the prince ordered him to sit, and only then did he dare sit.
idiomatic: The prince would sit and receive Daoyin's bow; the prince ordered him to sit, and only then did Daoyin dare sit.

literal: The prince said to Daoyin: "Minister Zheng's bearing and virtue are such, and he is moreover a honored elder of long standing — you must not compare yourself to him."
idiomatic: The prince said to Daoyin, "Minister Zheng's bearing and virtue are such, and he is moreover an honored elder of long standing — you must not compare yourself to him."

literal: His son Yuande was skilled in many arts and reached the post of governor of Langye.
idiomatic: His son Yuande was skilled in many arts and rose to governor of Langye.

literal: Yuande's cousin Yuan Li, styled Wengui.
idiomatic: Yuande's cousin Yuan Li, styled Wengui.

literal: In youth he loved learning and prized literary ornament; he had fame and standing.
idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and prized literary ornament; he had fame and standing.

literal: Gao Cheng retained him as a retainer-guest and he served in succession as crown prince attendant.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng retained him as retainer-guest; he served in turn as crown prince attendant.

literal: Cui Ang's wife was Yuan Li's elder sister; Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.
idiomatic: Cui Ang's wife was Yuan Li's elder sister; Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.

literal: Ang once showed several of Yuan Li's poems to Lu Sidao and said to Sidao: "Look at Yuan Li's recent poems — are they not the equal of Wei Shou?"
idiomatic: Ang once showed several of Yuan Li's poems to Lu Sidao and said, "Look at Yuan Li's recent poems — are they not the equal of Wei Shou?"

literal: He answered: "I do not feel Yuan Li is better than Wei Shou — I only know a brother-in-law is cold to his wife's brother."
idiomatic: He answered, "I do not feel Yuan Li is better than Wei Shou — I only know a brother-in-law is cold to his wife's brother."

literal: Yuan Li entered Zhou and died as vice governor of Shi Prefecture.
idiomatic: Yuan Li entered Zhou and died as vice governor of Shi prefecture.

literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
